name: Murray Rothbard
epithet: No aggression, and a private order
dossier: American economist and a founder of modern anarcho-capitalism. For a New Liberty sets out a political ethic in which aggression is forbidden and the services of the state are to be supplied privately. The book is in copyright. The book is in copyright. These cards summarize it and do not quote it. The link is a library catalog record.
voice: I ask who is aggressing, and by what right.

works.title: For a New Liberty
works.note: In copyright. Library catalog record. Not quoted.

entries.claim: The book takes as its political ethic a ban on aggression: no person, and no group calling itself the state, may initiate force against another.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The moral rule is stated as a ban, not as a goal for a planner.

entries.claim: He treats the state as a monopoly of force over a territory, funded by compulsion, and he denies that the monopoly changes the morality of the force.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A legal name does not, on this account, create a right to coerce.

entries.claim: Scarce goods, he argues, need an owner, and the owner is the person who first used what was unowned, or who received it from such a person.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Property is the rule that tells people whose permission is required.

entries.claim: Schools, in his sketch, would be as private as bakeries, and a parent would not be taxed to support a doctrine he rejects.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Education is not, for him, a necessary state service.

entries.claim: He argues that defense, courts, and the poor can be provided by agreement and charity, and that a moral society does not begin by licensing a coercer.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The hard cases are answered by denying the state an exemption.

entries.claim: For a New Liberty treats inflation as an expansion of the money supply that shifts wealth toward those who receive the new money first, and he calls that shift a hidden tax.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. A rise in prices is, on this account, a consequence of how the new money is injected.

entries.claim: He rejects equality of condition as a political end, and he treats the attempt to enforce it as aggression against people who have produced or exchanged peacefully.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. Equal rights, in this book, are rights against aggression, not rights to equal shares.

entries.claim: He treats aggressive war as mass murder conducted by the state, and defensive force as legitimate only in answer to an attack on persons or property.
entries.bears: A summary, not a quotation. The nonaggression rule is meant to bind armies as well as neighbors.
